title: Sheafification preserves ordinary pro-etale geometric stalks
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point], and $\mathcal P$ a presheaf of abelian groups on the small pro-etale site $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $\theta:\mathcal P\to\mathcal P^\#$ be its abelian sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Index both colimits below over the opposite of the category of pointed weakly etale neighbourhoods $(V,\bar v)$ of $\bar x$ defined in [def-weil-proetale-geometric-stalk]. Then the canonical homomorphism $\varinjlim_{(V,\bar v)}\mathcal P(V)\xrightarrow{\varinjlim\theta_V}\varinjlim_{(V,\bar v)}\mathcal P^\#(V)$ is an isomorphism, natural in $\mathcal P$.

source.place: Section Tag 0991 (section-points), Lemmas Tags 0F6B (lemma-cofinal-etale), 0F6C (lemma-geometric-lift-to-cover), and paragraph before Tag 0993 (lemma-classical-point); applied with Sites Tag 00Y8 (lemma-point-pushforward-sheaf), literature/stacks-project/sites.tex, clause (3)

proof.text: Use the small skeleton and larger universe already specified for the pointed-neighbourhood category $\mathcal N_{\bar x}$. Its opposite is filtered by [def-weil-proetale-geometric-stalk]. For any abelian presheaf $F$, form classes $[V,\bar v,s]$ of sections under restriction. Filteredness makes equality equivalent to equality after restriction to one common pointed refinement: a finite chain of generating restriction relations admits a common refinement, and the finitely many parallel arrows can then be equalized. Represent finitely many operands on a common refinement and add there. Common refinement and equalization show this is well-defined, and the group laws hold sectionwise. A compatible family of homomorphisms out of $F(V)$ descends uniquely to a homomorphism from this group of classes. Thus this group has the abelian colimit universal property; in particular every element is one section class and a class is zero exactly when it restricts to zero on a pointed refinement. Apply this construction to both presheaves in the statement.

source.place: Tag 0F6B (lemma-cofinal-etale), neighbourhood definition before it; elementary representative construction for abelian presheaves

proof.text: Let $\{V_i\to V\}$ cover a pointed neighbourhood $(V,\bar v)$. Base change this cover along $\bar v:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to V$. By [lem-galois-fpqc-covering-base-change] the pulled-back family is an fpqc cover $\{Z_i=V_i\times_V\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\}$; the fpqc covering condition ensures some $Z_i$ is nonempty. Its map to $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is weakly etale by [lem-weil-pbc-weakly-etale-composition-base-change]. Choose a point of $Z_i$ and an affine open $W=\operatorname{Spec}B$ containing it. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-weakly-etale-source-locality] to an open covering of $Z_i$ containing $W$, so $W\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is weakly etale. The affine equivalence in [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra] makes $B/\Omega$ a weakly etale algebra. By [lem-weil-pbc-weak-etale-field], its residue field at the chosen point is separable algebraic over $\Omega$. Since $\Omega$ is algebraically closed it is separably closed (each nonconstant separable polynomial is a nonconstant polynomial); [lem-weil-pbc-separable-extension-embeds-separably-closed] gives an $\Omega$-embedding of that residue field into $\Omega$. The geometric-point description and affine-spectrum functoriality give $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to W\to Z_i\to V_i$. The fibre-product equation says its composite to $V$ is exactly the fixed $\bar v$, with the same field $\Omega$. Thus $(V_i,\bar v_i)\to(V,\bar v)$ is a pointed refinement. Its structure map to $X$ is weakly etale by composition. The selected $V_i$ is an original site object; the auxiliary fibre and affine open are bounded schemes, and the lift has the original field $\Omega$. If $r:V_i^{\mathrm{sk}}\xrightarrow{\sim}V_i$ is the chosen $X$-isomorphism from its skeleton representative, use the lift $r^{-1}\circ\bar v_i$ and the covering arrow $V_i^{\mathrm{sk}}\xrightarrow{r}V_i\to V$; their composite is $\bar v$. Restriction along $r$ is an isomorphism on presheaf sections since its inverse is restriction along $r^{-1}$.

source.place: Tag 0F6C (lemma-geometric-lift-to-cover); expanded via more-algebra.tex Tag 092Q (lemma-absolutely-flat-over-field), more-morphisms.tex Tags 094S and 094U, and fields.tex Tag 09GU

proof.text: Write $S=\mathcal P^\#$, $\theta:\mathcal P\to S$, and $\eta:S\to S^\#$ for the two units. By [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], the identity of the sheaf $S$ factors as $b\eta=\mathrm{id}_S$ for a unique $b:S^\#\to S$. Both $\eta b$ and $\mathrm{id}_{S^\#}$ have composite $\eta$ with $\eta$, so uniqueness of extension from $S$ to the sheaf $S^\#$ gives $\eta b=\mathrm{id}_{S^\#}$. The induced map $\theta^\#:S\to S^\#$ is characterized by $\theta^\#\theta=\eta\theta$, and uniqueness of extension from $\mathcal P$ gives $\theta^\#=\eta$. Hence $\theta^\#$ is an isomorphism. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-iso-locally-bijective] to $\theta$: every section of $S$ lifts to $\mathcal P$ on a covering, and any two sections of $\mathcal P$ with equal images agree on a covering. The cited theorem is for abelian presheaves, so no comparison between set-valued and abelian sheafification is needed.

source.place: Tags 00WH (proposition-sheafification-adjoint) and 00WK (lemma-sections-sheafification); abelian local-bijectivity equivalence supplied by the cited general-site Mathlib leaf: CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.W_iff_isLocallyBijective, Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/LocallyBijective.lean:114-158, and CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.W_iff, Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/Localization.lean:76-82. proof.text: For a class $[V,\bar v,t]$ in the target colimit, Step 3 gives a cover $\{V_i\to V\}$ and sections $s_i\in\mathcal P(V_i)$ such that $\theta(s_i)=t|_{V_i}$. Step 2 supplies an index $i$ and a lift of the fixed geometric point to $V_i$. The restriction relation in Step 1 identifies $[V,\bar v,t]$ with $[V_i,\bar v_i,\theta(s_i)]$, the image of $[V_i,\bar v_i,s_i]$. Hence the canonical homomorphism is surjective.

source.place: Tag 0F6C and sites.tex Tag 00Y8 (lemma-point-pushforward-sheaf), clause (3); explicit local-representative proof

proof.text: If the image of $[V,\bar v,s]$ is zero, Step 1 supplies a pointed refinement $(W,\bar w)\to(V,\bar v)$ on which $\theta(s|_W)=0$. Step 3 applied to $s|_W$ and $0$ gives a cover $\{W_j\to W\}$ on which $s$ restricts to zero. Step 2 lifts the fixed $\bar w$ to one $W_j$. The original class is therefore zero by its restriction relation. The kernel is zero, so the canonical homomorphism is injective. Combined with Step 4 this is a group isomorphism: its inverse is additive because unique preimages of $a,b$ have sum the unique preimage of $a+b$.

source.place: Tag 0F6C and sites.tex Tag 00Y8 (lemma-point-pushforward-sheaf), clause (3); explicit zero-class proof

proof.text: For a morphism $a:\mathcal P\to\mathcal Q$, the sheafification universal property gives the map $a^\#:\mathcal P^\#\to\mathcal Q^\#$ characterized by $a^\#\theta_{\mathcal P}=\theta_{\mathcal Q}a$. On a representative $[V,\bar v,s]$, both paths around the stalk comparison square give $[V,\bar v,\theta_{\mathcal Q,V}(a_V(s))]$. Representatives generate the colimits by Step 1, so the square commutes. Since the components are isomorphisms by Steps 4–5, their inverses also commute (compose this square with the inverse components). This proves the claimed naturality.
